Combat mechanic.A1: Avatar War is a turn-based strategy game where you command a main character and eight avatars in a 3×3 formation, aiming to defeat the enemy’s main character while protecting your own. Teams alternate turns, with the higher-AP team acting first and action slots gradually increasing from two to four, then five. Reposition your characters, defend to pass an action slot to an ally, or commit to an attack or skill. Every move costs AP, and pushing a character into negative AP can secure an immediate advantage at the cost of delaying their next opportunity to act. Victory depends on teamwork, positioning, and timing.
Combat mechanic.C4: One team's opportunity to act before control passes to the opposing team.
Combat mechanic.C5: A transferable opportunity to act, separate from its holder and AP.
Combat mechanic.C6: Action Points. AP may become negative through action costs or modifiers.
Combat mechanic.C7: One team's turn in the battle-wide sequence. Each team turn advances the global turn counter by 1.
Combat mechanic.C8: One specific team's opportunity to act. One team turn equals one global turn; it does not include the opposing team's turn.
Combat mechanic.C9: Compare the highest individual AP value on each team at the start of battle. The team with the higher value acts first.
Combat mechanic.C10: If both teams have the same highest AP value, randomly determine the starting team.
Combat mechanic.C11: The two teams take turns alternately. Team A below denotes the starting team.
Combat mechanic.C12: Team A: maximum 2 initial action slots.
Combat mechanic.C13: Team B: maximum 2 initial action slots.
Combat mechanic.C14: Team A: maximum 4 initial action slots.
Combat mechanic.C15: Team B: maximum 4 initial action slots.
Combat mechanic.C16: The acting team receives a maximum of 5 initial action slots per team turn.
Combat mechanic.C17: AP recovers at the beginning of the acting team's turn, before initial action slots are assigned.
Combat mechanic.C18: Only the acting team receives default AP recovery.
Combat mechanic.C19: Specific modifiers may change AP recovery or AP during a turn.
Combat mechanic.C20: A character must have at least 100 AP to receive an initial action slot.
Combat mechanic.C21: If eligible characters exceed the slot limit, prioritize characters with higher current AP.
Combat mechanic.C22: Randomly resolve equal-AP ties when selecting initial slot holders.
Combat mechanic.C23: Assign one initial action slot to each selected character.
Combat mechanic.C24: The initial slot count is determined at the beginning of the turn. No additional slots are created during that turn.
Combat mechanic.C25: If fewer characters qualify than the turn's slot limit, assign one initial action slot to each qualifying character. Later AP changes do not increase the initial slot count.
Combat mechanic.C26: If no character qualifies, the turn ends and control passes to the opposing team.
Combat mechanic.C27: Later AP changes do not revoke an assigned slot.
Combat mechanic.C28: The holder may continue acting with less than 100 AP or negative AP until the slot is transferred, ended, or interrupted.
Combat mechanic.C29: A normal attack costs 100 AP. Modifiers may affect the cost or resulting AP.
Combat mechanic.C30: Attacking ends the current action slot.
Combat mechanic.C31: AP cost depends on the skill. A character may use a skill costing more than their current AP, resulting in negative AP.
Combat mechanic.C32: Using a skill ends the current action slot.
Combat mechanic.C33: Each character involved in a position swap loses 50 AP.
Combat mechanic.C34: A position swap is allowed with a character who has less than 50 AP. Their AP may become negative.
Combat mechanic.C35: The initiating character retains the current action slot.
Combat mechanic.C36: Position swaps are unlimited within the current action slot, including when the holder has negative AP.
Combat mechanic.C37: Being swapped does not itself consume or transfer the swap partner's action slot.
Combat mechanic.C39: Defending transfers the existing action slot to another eligible character. It does not create or end that slot.
Combat mechanic.C40: A character in the defending state cannot receive another action slot during the same team turn.
Combat mechanic.C41: A recipient may also defend and transfer the same slot again.
Combat mechanic.C42: If no other eligible character can receive the transfer, only the defending character's current action slot ends. Other active slots remain unaffected.
Combat mechanic.C43: While in defend state, stat defense effectivenes and skill defense effectiveness + 50%
Combat mechanic.C44: Defend state end after 2 turns, at turn start (the next turn of this team)
Combat mechanic.C45: Voluntarily ending the current action slot costs no AP.
Combat mechanic.C46: The slot ends without being transferred.
Combat mechanic.C47: A character who voluntarily ends a slot cannot receive another slot during the same team turn, regardless of AP.
Combat mechanic.C48: A recipient must have at least 100 AP at the moment of transfer.
Combat mechanic.C49: A character currently holding an action slot cannot receive a transferred slot.
Combat mechanic.C50: A recipient must not be in the defending state or have voluntarily ended a slot during the current team turn.
Combat mechanic.C51: A character who previously ended a slot by attacking or using a skill may receive another slot if currently eligible.
Combat mechanic.C52: AP changes may alter transfer eligibility, but do not revoke held slots or create new slots.
Combat mechanic.C53: If the holder dies, is stunned, or suffers another slot-interrupting effect before transferring the slot, that slot is lost and cannot be transferred afterward.
Combat mechanic.C54: The team turn ends when no active action slots remain.
Combat mechanic.C55: A failed defensive transfer ends the team turn only if no active action slots remain.
Combat mechanic.C56: A turn with no actions still counts toward the opening turn sequence.
Combat mechanic.C57: The battle-ending condition takes priority over remaining actions and slots.
Combat mechanic.C58: Defeat the opposing team's main character to win.
Combat mechanic.C59: Unless explicitly stated otherwise, duration is measured in global turns.
Combat mechanic.C60: An effect becomes active when applied. Its application turn counts as the first turn of its duration, regardless of when during that turn it is applied.
Combat mechanic.C61: An effect with duration D, applied on global turn T, remains active through global turn T + D − 1 and expires at the end of that turn.
Combat mechanic.C62: For effects that allow refreshing, reapplication on global turn R resets expiration to the end of global turn R + D − 1.
Combat mechanic.C63: An effect must already be active when its trigger occurs. Applying an effect after that trigger does not activate it retroactively.
Combat mechanic.C64: A skill's duration applies to all timed effects it applies, unless an effect explicitly specifies a different duration.
Combat mechanic.C65: Each character tracks a separate remaining cooldown for each skill, measured in global turns and governed by the Effect Duration rules.
Combat mechanic.C66: At battle initialization, set each skill's remaining cooldown to its applicable cooldown duration. Each team's initial countdown begins on its first team turn.
Combat mechanic.C67: When a skill cast is committed, set its remaining cooldown to the applicable cooldown duration before resolving its effects. The casting turn counts as the first cooldown turn.
Combat mechanic.C68: A skill is ready when its remaining cooldown reaches 0. Readiness does not bypass MP requirements, usage conditions, or action-slot requirements where applicable.
Combat mechanic.C69: If a skill becomes ready during a team turn through an explicit cooldown-reduction effect, it may be used again that turn, subject to its normal requirements. Each cast starts a new cooldown.
Combat mechanic.C70: Each team's first default cooldown recovery occurs at the end of its first team turn. Thereafter, recovery occurs at the end of every global turn, including the opposing team's turns.
Combat mechanic.C71: Each default recovery reduces remaining cooldown by 1. Remaining cooldown cannot fall below 0; excess recovery is discarded.
Combat mechanic.C72: Default recovery applies to all skills of living characters, regardless of AP or action eligibility. Turns without actions still count.
Combat mechanic.C73: Additional actions, hits, or casts do not grant additional default recovery. Recovery grants no AP or action slots.
Combat mechanic.C74: Effects that directly change remaining cooldown apply immediately, according to their specified timing and scope.
Combat mechanic.C75: Changes to cooldown duration affect subsequent cooldown assignments. They do not change an existing remaining cooldown unless explicitly stated.
Combat mechanic.C76: Changes to cooldown recovery affect subsequent recovery events according to their specified amount, timing, and scope.

Termynology.E2: The character's health. Current HP decreases when taking damage; the character is defeated when it reaches 0. Max HP defines the maximum health capacity.
Termynology.E3: A resource consumed by skills that require MP. Current MP is the available amount; Max MP defines the maximum capacity.
Termynology.E4: The character's base offensive power, used to calculate damage for attacks and skills that scale with Attack.
Termynology.E5: The character's ability to reduce incoming damage from normal attacks, according to the normal attack damage formula. Does not apply to skill damage.
Termynology.E6: The character's offensive power used to calculate damage for skills that scale with Skill Attack. Does not apply to normal attack damage.
Termynology.E7: The character's ability to reduce incoming skill damage, according to the applicable skill damage formula.
Termynology.E8: The character's current action resource. At least 100 AP is required to receive an action slot. Action costs and modifiers change AP, which may become negative.
Termynology.E9: The amount of AP the character normally recovers at the beginning of their team's turn, before initial action slots are assigned.
Termynology.E10: A resource spent to increase a skill's level.
Termynology.E11: The probability that an eligible hit becomes a critical hit.
Termynology.E12: The additional damage dealt by a critical hit compared with an equivalent non-critical hit. A 50% bonus means 150% of normal damage.
Termynology.E13: Determines the number of hits generated by one attack. Each full 100% grants one guaranteed hit; the remaining percentage is the chance of one additional hit. For example, 250% grants two guaranteed hits and a 50% chance of a third. These hits belong to the same action and do not create additional action slots.
Termynology.E14: The character's accuracy percentage, combined with the target's Evasion to calculate the final hit chance.
Termynology.E15: The character's evasion percentage, combined with the attacker's Accuracy to calculate the final hit chance.
Termynology.E16: Increases healing and HP regeneration received. Defaults to 0%. Base contributions stack additively. A final value of 20% increases healing received by 20%.
Termynology.E17: A multiplier applied to Total Stats to determine their Final values. It does not multiply itself. A value of 100% leaves values unchanged; 120% multiplies them by 1.2.
Termynology.E18: The chance for each landed normal-attack hit to ignore the target's Defense entirely. Roll independently for each hit. Does not apply to skills.
Termynology.E21: A random value sampled uniformly from 0 inclusive to 1 exclusive. Each roll is independent.
Termynology.E22: A probability check succeeds when the roll value is strictly less than the checked probability P. Probabilities of 0% or lower always fail; probabilities of 100% or higher always succeed.
Termynology.E23: Checks whether a hit lands by comparing a random roll with the calculated Hit Chance.
Termynology.E24: Checks whether an eligible landed hit becomes critical by comparing a separate random roll with the attacker's Final Critical Hit Chance.
Termynology.E25: Determines the number of hits generated by an attack. Full hundreds grant guaranteed hits; the fractional remainder determines the chance of one additional hit. Requires a non-negative Final Multi-Hit Rate.
Termynology.E26: A hidden stat calculated for each attack against a target. It determines the probability of a hit and is not displayed on the character stat panel.
Termynology.E27: The actual damage received from a normal attack after mitigation is applied.
Termynology.E28: The percentage of incoming normal attack damage prevented. For example, 40% Mitigation means the character receives 60% of the incoming normal attack damage.
Termynology.E29: The actual damage received from a skill after skill mitigation is applied.
Termynology.E30: The percentage of incoming skill damage prevented. For example, 40% Skill Mitigation means the character receives 60% of the incoming skill damage.
Termynology.E31: A fixed reference value used to express and compare the numerical scale of stats. Stat values may be defined as multiples of K; their actual gameplay effectiveness depends on the applicable formulas.
Termynology.E36: A numerical attribute or parameter that describes a property of a character, item, or skill and is used to determine gameplay outcomes.
Termynology.E37: The original value of a stat belonging to a character, before contributions from items, skills, or other sources and before any modifiers are applied.
Termynology.E38: The original value of a stat belonging to an item, before any modifiers are applied.
Termynology.E39: The original value of a stat belonging to a skill, before any modifiers are applied.
Termynology.E40: The sum of all base contributions to the same stat type from characters, items, skills, and other applicable sources.
Termynology.E41: The combined value of a stat before Stat Effectiveness is applied.
Termynology.E42: The resulting value of a stat after Stat Effectiveness is applied to its Total Stat. Stat Effectiveness itself is excluded from this multiplication.
Termynology.E43: The amount added to or subtracted from a stat, calculated by multiplying its Total Base Stat by the applicable percentage modifier.
Termynology.E44: The amount added to or subtracted from a stat by character-sourced percentage modifiers, calculated using its Total Base Stat.
Termynology.E45: The amount added to or subtracted from a stat by item-sourced percentage modifiers, calculated using its Total Base Stat, not the item's own Base Stat.
Termynology.E46: The amount added to or subtracted from a stat by skill-sourced percentage modifiers, calculated using its Total Base Stat.
Termynology.D47: T_INC_X = Σ Increased Contributions = T_B_X × T_X_MOD
Termynology.E47: The sum of all increases and decreases to the same stat type, calculated from its Total Base Stat and applicable percentage modifiers.
Termynology.E48: A percentage adjustment that increases or decreases a specified reference value.
Termynology.E49: A percentage adjustment applied to the Total Base Stat of the same stat type. Its source does not change the reference value.
Termynology.E50: A Stat Modifier provided by a character, applied to the Total Base Stat of the same stat type.
Termynology.E51: A Stat Modifier provided by an item, applied to the Total Base Stat of the same stat type, not the item's own Base Stat.
Termynology.E52: A Stat Modifier provided by a skill, applied to the Total Base Stat of the same stat type.
Termynology.E53: The sum of all applicable Stat Modifiers for the same stat type. Modifiers stack additively, not multiplicatively.
Termynology.E54: A specified event that initiates a check to activate an effect. The effect activates only if its required conditions and probability check are satisfied.
Termynology.E55: A probability that an effect activates when its trigger event occurs and all required conditions are satisfied. A separate roll is performed for each eligible trigger occurrence.
Termynology.E56: The character's total skill-point budget: base skill points plus total flat bonuses from applicable sources.
Termynology.E57: The level of an individual skill obtained through allocation. Each allocated skill point grants 1 base skill level, subject to its allocation limit. Total points allocated across skills cannot exceed F_SP.
Termynology.E58: The effective level of an individual skill: allocated base level plus total flat level bonuses. Bonus levels consume no skill points and may exceed the base allocation limit.
Termynology.E59: The number of Stun Count stacks required to stun the character.
Termynology.E62: An offensive action that generates hits based on Multi-Hit Rate. Uses the weapon’s targeting and area rules.
Termynology.E63: A skill use that directly attacks enemies. Uses the skill’s own targeting, area, and damage rules. Does not generate hits or use Multi-Hit Rate.
Termynology.E64: An individual strike generated by a normal attack. Each affected recipient receives a separate hit check. A hit may land or miss.
Termynology.E65: A character explicitly selected as a primary recipient of an attack or skill. Characters affected only by its area are secondary recipients, not selected targets.
Termynology.E66: To commit a skill use after meeting its requirements, before resolving its effects. Applies to damaging, healing, buffing, and debuffing skills.
Termynology.E67: Triggers once per normal attack that lands at least one hit, regardless of the number of hits or recipients struck.
Termynology.E68: Triggers once per offensive cast that directly strikes at least one enemy, regardless of the number of recipients struck.
Termynology.E69: Triggers each time a normal-attack hit lands on a recipient.
Termynology.E70: Triggers once when the character commits a normal attack or skill with one or more selected primary targets, regardless of the outcome.
Termynology.E71: Triggers once when the character commits a valid skill use, before its effects resolve.
Termynology.E72: Triggers once per incoming normal attack that lands at least one hit on the character, regardless of the number of hits.
Termynology.E73: Triggers once per offensive cast that directly strikes the character.
Termynology.E74: Triggers separately for each normal-attack hit that lands on the character.
Termynology.E75: Triggers once when the character is selected as a primary target of a committed normal attack or skill, regardless of the outcome.
Termynology.E76: Triggers once per skill use that successfully applies a direct effect to the character, including damage, healing, buffs, or debuffs. Includes primary and secondary recipients.
Termynology.E77: Only normal attacks generate hits. Skills do not generate hits.
Termynology.E78: Targeting occurs when an action is committed. Previewing or hovering over a target does not count. Area effects do not count as selecting additional primary targets.
Termynology.E79: A passive skill with an automatic casting mechanism can trigger When Casting. A passive stat bonus alone is not a cast.
Termynology.E80: Damage-over-time ticks and transferred damage do not create new attacks, hits, or casts, and do not trigger the receiving events listed above. Applying a damage-over-time effect initially can trigger When Affected by a Skill.
Termynology.E81: Action-level triggers occur once per action. Recipient-level triggers are checked separately for each qualifying character.
Termynology.E82: Automatically commits a skill cast when its specified trigger occurs and all casting requirements are met. Requires no manual input or action slot. Applies the skill’s specified costs, cooldown, targeting, and effects, and triggers When Casting.

status.C18: Prevents receiving action slots and performing voluntary actions, including attacks, defending, swaps, and active skills. Sets Character Base AP Recovery to 0. Passive skills remain usable.
status.C19: Has no direct effect. Each target can gain at most 1 Stun Count stack per global turn, regardless of the number of hits or sources. status.C20: The number of Stun Count stacks required to trigger Stun.
status.C21: Prevents receiving action slots and performing voluntary actions, including attacks, defending, swaps, and active skills. Passive skills remain usable.
status.C22: Reduces AP Recovery and Multi-Hit Rate. Stackable. Maximum 5 stacks
status.C27: Grants immunity to all damage and negative statuses.
status.C29: Allows the character to act, but prevents manual control.
